churn_details:
We are convinced Microsoft folded GSA into their broader Entra Suite renewal at little or no additional cost. It looks to us like the customer essentially got it for free, which gave them an easy way to justify retiring Zscaler without feeling any real financial impact.From our perspective, this was largely a cost and convenience decision. The security rationale they presented did not hold up, and many of their claims were simply incorrect.We also feel they allowed end users to steer the decision rather than anchoring it on proper security architecture or long term risk posture. That’s what makes the justification frustrating for us.We fully expect they’ll experience issues with Microsoft’s product. We’ve seen this pattern before. Once the performance gaps and security limitations show up, we anticipate they will reconsider and eventually come back.We’ve done this before with other accounts. We provide a soft landing, let them run their course, and when things start breaking downstream, they return. Check in Dec.CMS Meeting Minutes: lee and Justin w/ Raz Razvan, Leon
1. Customer Overview & Core FeedbackPrimary Issue RaisedLongstanding performance problems with internet access when ZIA was enabled.Users experienced click and wait behavior on basic web browsing.Performance with Zscaler vs Microsoft GSA was described as “a tenfold” difference.Customer repeatedly raised concerns over several years (tickets, diagnostics, escalations).Customer TestingTested with ZIA disabled, ZPA disabled, various diagnostics with Zscaler engineering.Zscaler advised against speed tests; however, issues were visible even during normal browsing.Customer noted consistent, repeatable performance improvements when using Microsoft GSA instead.Experience ComparisonZscaler: Strong security, ZDX visibility, mature product, robust reporting.Microsoft GSA: Superior end user performance, seamless integration with conditional access policies, continuous authentication.Some Zscaler capabilities (ZDX, CIPA alignment) exceed Microsoft’s current maturity, but customer sees Microsoft catching up.2. Customer Security & Architecture PositionConditional Access & Continuous AuthenticationCustomer requires conditional access based on device and user risk levels managed inside Microsoft Entra.Customer already uses Microsoft identity stack to secure:Internal appsAzure-hosted applicationsSharePointExchange OnlineCustomer chose to disable Zscaler’s own risk-based access controls because:They did not want to manage two separate policy stacks.They rely on Microsoft’s ecosystem as the single source of truth.Integrations available with Zscaler were not instantaneous or granular enough for their needs.Security Capability Trade-offsCustomer acknowledges:Microsoft is behind Zscaler in ZDX telemetry and reporting.Private preview features (TLS inspection, sandboxing, domain filtering) are still evolving.Customer is nonetheless prioritizing architectural integration over best-in-class standalone security controls.Environment CharacteristicsCustomer is nearly 100 percent Microsoft.No meaningful SaaS or app footprint on AWS aside from key vaults.End user and application environment is not multi-cloud.3. Rationale for Migration to Microsoft GSAKey DriversUser experience and performance were the decisive factors.Full integration with Microsoft identity, conditional access, and risk scoring.Alignment with their existing security tooling and policy architecture.Already purchased Entra Suite, which includes GSA, during a wider Microsoft renewal.Cost is embedded into other Microsoft workloads, reducing incremental spend.Evaluation ProcessDid not run a competitive RFP.Did not review Netskope or other security vendors.Only evaluated Microsoft and Zscaler due to maturity gap historically.DecisionCustomer is moving forward with Microsoft GSA and will fully migrate away from Zscaler.
